blocks.text: A Constitution lays out certain ideals that form the basis of the kind of country a nation aspires to be.
Tradition of Constitution began in: USA (in 1787).
Independence of USA: 4th July 1776.
While all democratic countries are likely to have a Constitution, it is not necessary that all countries that have a Constitution are democratic.
Democratic Government: A democratic government is a form of government in which power is held by the people and exercised through their elected representatives.
Forms of Government:
Communist: Source or means of production controlled by government. E.g. China.
Oligarchic: A government ruled by a few. E.g. China, Russia.
Monarchic: A government by a single person specifically King or a monarch. E.g. Saudi Arabia, UK.
Totalitarian: It refers to total control over lives of citizens by whoever is ruling E.g. North Korea.
1928: The early draft of the Indian Constitution (Nehru Report) was submitted by the All Parties Conference at Lucknow chaired by Motilal Nehru.
1934: M. N. Roy first proposed the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India.
1935: The Indian National Congress officially demanded a Constitutional Assembly.

1938: Jawaharlal Nehru, on behalf of the INC, declared that 'the Constitution of free India must be framed without outside interference, by a Constituent Assembly elected on the basis of adult franchise'.
Reason: Ongoing World War II (1939-1945)
1. August Offer: 1940
2. Cripps Proposal: 1942
3. Wavell Plan: 1945

4. Cabinet Mission Plan: 1946 > with 3 British Cabinet members: Pethick-Lawrence (chairman), Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander. Only Cabinet Mission Plan was accepted by both the Congress and the Muslim League, hence Constituent Assembly was formed according to it.
Note: This topic is discussed in detail in Modern history.
Reasons for Rejection of Former ones
Congress demanded Purna Swaraj, but Britishers offered Dominion Status.
Provisions of Cabinet Mission Plan
Total seats: 389
1. Elected Members: 296 — represented British India.
Out of 296:
292 members came from Governor's Provinces (11 provinces in total).
4members came from Chief Commissioner's Provinces.
(4 provinces)
2. Nominated Members: 93 — represented Princely States (members to be nominated by rulers of that princely state).
Seats allocated to each British province were to be divided among three principal communities: Muslim, Sikh and General.
One seat was to be allotted per 1 million population.
It was partly elected and partly nominated.
Method of election (Indirect Elections): Proportional Representation + Single Transferable Vote.
Elections held in: July-August 1946.
Results: Majority: Congress (INC): 208 seats
Muslim League: 73 seats
Independent: 15 seats
After boycott of Muslim League, Remaining seats: 299 (after partition).
On 2nd September 1946: The Interim Government of India was formed. It lasted until India's independence on 15th August 1947, and the Partition of the country into India and Pakistan.
President of the Executive Council (Viceroy and Governor-General of India): Viscount Wavell (till Feb 1947)
Lord Mountbatten (from Feb 1947)
> Commander-in-Chief: Sir Claude Auchinleck — Vice President, also in charge of External Affairs and Commonwealth Relations: Jawaharlal Nehru (INC)
> Home Affairs, Information and Broadcasting: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (INC)
~> Agriculture and Food: Rajendra Prasad (INC)
Commerce: Ibrahim Ismail Chundrigar (ML)
Defence: Baldev Singh (INC)
~ Finance: Liaquat Ali Khan (ML) (1st PM of Pakistan)
Health: Ghazanfar Ali Khan (ML) aan Jagjivan Ram (INC)
Law: Jogendra Nath Mandal (ML)
Education and Arts: C. Rajagopalachari (INC)
Railways and Communication, Post and Air: Abdur Rab Nishtar (ML)
Industries and Supplies: John Mathai (INC)
The 1st Interim National Government was announced on 24th Aug 1946.

The Objective Resolution, moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946 in the Constituent Assembly, laid the fundamental principles and philosophy for the Indian Constitution & was adopted on 22 Jan 1947.

Drafts of Constituent Assembly
21 Feb 1948: First draft was published. It took 8 months for people of India to discuss.
21 Oct 1948:2nd draft
4 Nov 1948:B. R. Ambedkar introduced the final draft before Constituent Assembly.

B.R. Ambedkar was elected to the Constituent assembly from Bengal (in place of Jogendranath Mandal) in July 1946 (before Partition), but after Partition he was elected from Bombay Presidency (after M.R. Jayakar resigned).
1st reading: 5 days (4th Nov 1948-9th Nov 1948).
2nd reading: 10 months and 3 days (15 Nov 1948-17 Oct
3rd reading: Completed on 26 Nov 1949.
211 members were present on the 1st day of the constituent assembly.
Total sessions held: 11 sessions for 165 days.
Total time taken for drafting the Constitution: 2 years 11 months 18 days.
No. of members who signed constitution on 24th Jan 1950- 284 (including 15 female members).
Budget: 64 lakhs (to frame the Constitution).
1st Session: 9-23rd December 1946
10th Session: 6-17th October 1949
11th Session: 14-26th November 1949 (also the last session).
26th November 1949: Constitution was adopted (this day is also celebrated as the "Constitution Day")
Constitution was enforced/Commenced on 26th January 1950, Celebrated as Republic Day. But few provisions of the constitution that came into force on 26th November 1949 were:
E • • Elections (Article 324-329)
Citizenship (Article 5-9)
The reason for choosing this date is because on the same day in 1930 Purna Swaraj day was celebrated following the Lahore session of the Congress (1929).
Originally, our Constitution consisted of 395 Articles, 8 Schedules, 22 Parts and a Preamble.
Functions of the Constituent Assembly other than Making of the Constitution
Ist meeting: 9 Dec 1946
Whenever the assembly met as the constituent body it was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad and when it met as the legislative body it was chaired by G.V. Mavalankar.
Temporary President (before elections): Dr. Sachchida- nanda Sinha — President (after elections): Dr. Rajendra Prasad — Vice President: V. T. Krishnamachari and H. C. Mukherjee
It functioned as the 'First Parliament of India'.
It adopted National Flag on 22 July, 1947
It adopted National Anthem ("Jana Gana Mana" by · Rabindranath Tagore) and National Song ("Vande Mataram"— by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee) on 24 January, 1950.
It ratified India's membership of the Commonwealth in May 1949.
Elected Dr. Rajendra Prasad as the Ist President of India on 26 Jan 1950.
Some more Significant facts to know:
Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan was one of the speakers after Jawaharlal Nehru to address the Parliament on the midnight of 15th Aug 1947.
The Socialist Party called for the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly and its re-election by adult suffrage.
B.R. Ambedkar stated "on the 26th Jan 1950, we are going to enter a life of contradictions. In politics we will have equality and in social and economic life we will have inequality."
Designer of Indian National Flag-Pingali Venkayya (Approved by Mahatma Gandhi in a congress meeting in Vijayawada in 1921).
Somnath Lehri said "Constituent assembly was a conspiracy of Britishers" (book-Samyobad) and Somnath Lehri was a writer and editor of the left newspaper Swadhinata.
HM Seervai - Authored book 'Constitutional law of India'- A comprehensive commentary on the Indian Constitution.
The printed records of the Constituent assembly discussions were compiled into 12 Volumes.
Constitution Calligraphers:
English: Prem Bihari Narain Raizada Hindi: Vasant Krishan Vaidya
Constitution decorated by: Nand Lal Bose and Beohar Rammanohar Sinha
Secretary of Constituent Assembly: H. V. Iyengar
India's constitution is the largest written constitution, its symbol is the Elephant.
Language of the Constitution: English
